contexts.text: Whatever man has once acquired, remains.
His life in the world remains with him...
Not the least evil which man has thought or actually done is blotted out, but it all remains.
All the good which man has thought and done... remains.
Everything of the first Rational remains...
All the affections and derivative thoughts... remain after death.
Remain here with the donkey () = separation...
Let the girl remain with us () = detention...
It is always provided that something of the Church remains.
This evil remains to eternity. Whereas the evil not of fault... does indeed remain, but only in externals...
Evil and falsity are not separated from the Angels; but it all remains with them...
Such as man's Natural has been formed in the world, such it remains.
It is this interior life which... remains after death.
According to (the ends) his life remains.
For the life of everyone remains (there). AC 5718:end.
To cause to remain = to be separated.
Applications to falsities and evils, once impressed on any Scientific, remain.
All the truth and good ever given to man. Spirit, or Angel, remain.
As man dies, so he remains.
After death his life follows him, and remains in the state...
His life awaits everyone; not his civil life which appeared... but his spiritual life...
What is compulsory does not remain... But the things appropriated (in freedom) remain.
(Thus) all things which enter with man, remain. Signified, Explained.
The desire to do evil always remains.
What is effected by both (the Voluntary and the Intellectual) remains...
Truths once made of faith, remain, and cannot be eradicated.
Hence man after death remains as he has been made truth and good.
Man remains to eternity such as is his predominant affection. Explained.
That which is in the spirit of man... remains after death.
That man after death remains to eternity such as he is as to his reigning will or love. Explained.
That faith does not remain [with] man if it is not from heavenly love. Explained.
That love in act is that which remains. Explained.
That alone remains in the spirit of man which has entered into his love.
To abide in the Lord = to be in love to Him.
He then remains such as has been his life (here); that is, such as has been his reigning love.
That whatever man does from freedom according to his thought... remains. General article.
When it is removed, it is transferred... to the circumferences... This is meant by its being said that it remains.
For everyone's life awaits him, and thence his lot.
That whatever man thinks, speaks, or acts from the will... remains. Explained.
All evils or sins remain; and, when remitted, are removed to the sides.
What man does from himself in freedom, remains to eternity; but what he does from fear does not remain.
That one's own love remains with everyone after death. Explained.
That the love of the sex remains with every man after death, such as it had been interiorly... Explained.
That conjugial love in like manner remains... Explained.
That everything spiritual of the Church which enters in freedom... remains. General article.
The spiritual things of the Word and Church which man imbibes from love, and which, the understanding confirms, remain with man; but not so civil and political things. Explained.
For that which is not received by man from free will does not remain. General article.
That... unless man in part removes evils by repentance, he remains in them; and he who remains in them cannot be saved. General article.
All evil which man has appropriated to himself actually, remains.
What has once been acquired, remains...
All states, thoughts, speeches, and acts, in like manner remain...
Falsities still remain, although removed by truths...
(What they acquire after death) does not remain...
